author: Brett
description: Brett's Box is a maker's lab notebook: an old Roomba turned into a mapping robot, a self-hosted homelab, and a 3D printer that keeps all of it held together.
blog_description: Build notes from the bench: what I tried, what broke, what I measured and what finally worked.

vslam.alt: Screen recording of the Roomba's web dashboard while it explores on its own: a grey-scale camera view on the left, and on the right a top-down map that grows as the robot drives, with its planned path drawn in purple and obstacles in red.
vslam.caption: The robot exploring on its own. Left: what the camera sees. Right: the map it builds as it goes, with the planned path in purple and obstacles in red.

twin.alt: Isaac Sim recording of the simulated Roomba driving through the simulated house on its own. A follow camera shows the robot on the carpet; panels on the right show the robot's camera view and a depth heat map, red for near and blue for far, with a legend from 0.3 to 7 metres.
twin.caption: The robot's real software exploring the simulated house on its own. Right: what its camera sees, and the depth it gets, red near to blue far. Black is outside the camera's 0.3–7 m range.

people.alt: Isaac Sim recording of the simulated Roomba exploring the simulated house on its own while simulated people walk past it near a staircase railing. An inset in the corner shows the robot's own camera view from 13 cm above the floor.
people.caption: The robot's real software (cuVSLAM, Nav2 and the explorer) exploring the simulated house on its own while people walk past. Inset: what its camera sees.

swarm.alt: Side-by-side render of the Isaac Lab simulation: a grid of 4 by 4 metre tiles seen from above at an angle, each with a small simulated Roomba among walls, furniture, railings and drops. Text at the top of each half gives the counts. Left, before training: most robots stay in place with blue or red rings; 243 of 1,536 freed. Right, after training: many robots drive clear and turn green; 1,289 of 1,536 freed.
swarm.caption: A render of the actual Isaac Lab simulation, not robot footage, at 0.6× real time. Rings: blue driving, grey idle, red bump, green freed; the line is the last 4 s of driving. Just for this view, each tile holds one robot, walls are see-through, robots are brightened, and a freed robot pauses for 1.5 s before restarting.

unstuck.alt: Animated top-down drawing of two grids of nine small maps each. In every map a blue disc, the Roomba, starts stuck against walls, furniture or a stair drop. Left grid: today's recovery, where several robots stay stuck and one falls down the drop. Right grid: the learned skill, where most robots drive clear and get a green ring and a 'FREE in' time.
unstuck.caption: Drawn from logged Isaac Lab runs, not robot footage. The same stuck spots, first from the house's floor plans and then generated ones: today's recovery on the left, the learned skill on the right. A green ring means it reached 0.3 m of clear space.

explore.alt: Animated top-down drawing of two copies of the same house map filling in as a simulated robot explores, with orange frontier edges, numbered candidate goals and a pink star on the chosen one. Left: the explorer's rule. Right: the learned ranker. A coverage graph underneath compares the two over time.
explore.caption: Drawn from logged runs of the 2D simulator, not robot footage, at 30 times speed. The same start, with the rule on the left and the learned ranker on the right, first on one of the house's floor plans, then on a generated house it never trained on.

home.tagline: Robots, homelab and 3D printing, built at the bench and written down as I go.
home.intro: I like taking old hardware that most people would throw out and teaching it new tricks. This is my lab notebook: the wiring diagrams, the dead ends, the measurements and the small wins.
home.featured_summary: A 2007-era Roomba 550 with a Jetson Orin Nano and a stereo depth camera on its back. It builds a map of the house with visual SLAM, plans its own routes with Nav2 and explores rooms it has never seen.
home.video_caption: Live from the robot's dashboard: exploring and mapping on its own, no remote control.
now: Training navigation skills in simulation. The learned unstuck skill frees the simulated robot three times as often as today's recovery; nothing trained runs on the real robot yet.
Taking the robot's new Rust nodes on their first real drive: ten of them, a fraction of the CPU of the Python originals.
Recording test drives to compare the CPU (Basalt) and GPU (cuVSLAM) pipelines' maps side by side.
Wiring an ADS1115 pack-voltage monitor so the robot parks itself before the Ridgid pack runs flat.
Still hunting the cause of Charging Error 3 (next step: borrow an oscilloscope).
